original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, identify which edges of G correspond to the original segments of the underlying segment set S.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Open Problem 16: "Given a segment visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, identify the edges of G that correspond to segments of S."
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies that the input is the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, and that the task is to recover the distinguished subset of edges corresponding to the original segments in the underlying segment set S, rather than to solve the broader recognition or reconstruction problems.
missing_details: The paper assumes G is already known to be a segment visibility graph of some set S; deciding whether an arbitrary graph has such a realization is a separate problem (Section 3.1, Open Problem 12).
The underlying geometric object is a set S of disjoint line segments in the plane.
The vertices of G are the endpoints of the segments in S.

Besides the special segment-edges, G also contains visibility edges: two endpoints are adjacent when the straight segment joining them does not intersect any segment of S; this visibility notion does not allow passing through another endpoint or grazing along a segment.
The edges to be identified are exactly the special edges joining the two endpoints of each original segment of S, not all visibility edges.
Only the abstract graph G in adjacency-matrix form is given; the embedded segment visibility graph drawn on S is not part of the input.
The paper does not add a polynomial-time requirement to Open Problem 16; that complexity requirement appears in the neighboring Open Problem 15, not here.
The problem is narrower than full geometric reconstruction of S from G; reconstruction is treated separately in Section 3.1, Open Problem 14.
No algebraic ambient structure, degree condition, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' quantifier is involved here; the hidden assumptions are entirely geometric and graph-theoretic.
refined_question: Let S be a set of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane, and let G be its segment visibility graph: the vertices of G are the endpoints of the segments of S; two vertices u and v are adjacent if the straight segment uv does not intersect any segment of S (with visibility not allowed to pass through another endpoint or graze a segment), and, in addition, the two endpoints of each segment of S are joined by an edge. Given only the adjacency matrix of G, determine which edges of G are exactly the distinguished edges joining the two endpoints of the original segments of S.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s Open Problem 16, and it should be sharpened mainly by making the paper’s definition of a segment visibility graph explicit. Section 1 introduces segment visibility graphs for a set S of disjoint line segments in the plane and distinguishes ordinary visibility edges from the extra edges joining the endpoints of each segment. Section 3.1 then separates recognition, characterization, and reconstruction as different problems. In Section 3.2, after discussing Hamiltonian circuits in the embedded segment visibility graph and noting that only the abstract graph G may be given, the authors explicitly formulate Open Problem 16 asking to identify the edges of G that correspond to segments of S. Because the paper states this as a separate problem from both recognition and reconstruction, and because it does not impose a polynomial-time bound on Open Problem 16, the refined question should stay exactly at that level and not broaden into reconstruction, recognition, or algorithmic complexity claims.
